title: SentryOne labelled holdout case
description: One payment instruction, everything the detectors may read about it, and the label. Field names and enumerations are the ones in packages/core/src/domain.ts; this file never introduces a second shape. The runtime half of this contract is parseHoldoutCase in ./types.ts, and the two have to be edited together.

$schema.description: Relative path back to this file, so an editor validates the case as it is typed.

id.description: Stable slug. Named after the case, not numbered, so inserting one does not renumber the set.

title.description: One line a judge could read off the metrics page.

kind.description: positive: at least one detector should fire. negative: the case looks like fraud and is not. Stated rather than derived, so an empty expectedFindings cannot be mistaken for an unfinished case.

notes.description: Author's note. Ignored by the harness.

input.description: Everything the engine may read. Nothing outside this object exists for this case.

satEntries.description: The list rows in force for this case, as if a version had just been published.

sat49BisEntries.description: Article 49 Bis publications for this supplier. A separate statute from 69-B with one published outcome and no published clearing, so the two lists never share a row.

bankMirror.description: The company's own statement as the bank posted it. Absent means the mirror was not loaded and the reconciliation control says so instead of reading every payment as missing.

expectedFindings.description: One entry per detector at most. Matching is by detector, narrowed by state and severity when they are given. The explanation text is never compared.

because.description: Why this is the right label, in one sentence. Read out loud during review.

expectedLevel.description: How the line should read on the screen. Labelled from what the case is, not derived from expectedFindings: deriving it through the same rule table the engine uses would make the level matrix agree with itself and measure nothing.

rfc.description: Synthetic RFCs only. ADR-0002 keeps real RFCs to the read-only SAT lookup box, and a holdout case is the easiest place for one to slip in unnoticed.

instant.description: ISO 8601. Our ledger carries a real timestamp; Nessie carries dates with no time.

money.description: MXN in major units, at most two decimal places.

synthetic.description: Always true. The UI renders the watermark from this flag, never from a name.

findingState.description: Provable from documents, or needs a human check. Never an accusation.

confidence.description: The three words a line reads at. alerta: the documents say this payment is wrong. precaucion: something is open and a person checks. confiable: nothing is open.

sentAt.description: When the company marked the SPEI as sent. Absent while the payment is still pending, which is what separates not paid yet from paid and missing from the bank mirror.

establishedBy.description: The evidence that established this account. A new account is never trusted without one of these.

paymentMethod.description: PUE paid in one exhibition, PPD in instalments, which is when a complement follows.

paymentTotal.description: Monto of the Pago node: what left the bank in one transfer. paidAmount is this row's share of it.

operationNumber.description: NumOperacion. For a SPEI this is the clave de rastreo, which is how the CEP is located at Banxico.

publishedAt.description: DOF publication date of the oficio. The buyer's thirty natural days start here.

oficio.description: The resolution oficio, verbatim, which is the citation a clerk checks.

amount.description: Always positive. direction carries the sign.

raw.description: The original payload, kept verbatim so nothing is lost in normalisation.

beneficiaryRfc.description: Beneficiary RFC as the CEP reports it. Banks send NA when they have none.

numeroCertificado.description: Serial of the Banxico certificate the sello claims.

signatureValid.description: True only when the XML signature validated against the Banxico certificate.

signatureReason.description: Why signatureValid is what it is. unconfirmed_scheme reads as not verified in the UI, never as invalid.

xml.description: The raw signed XML, byte exact, because XMLDSig validates over the bytes.
